prompt: A hero section's label, headline, subtext, and button all render at the same 16px size, same weight, and same color. What problem does this create?
choices: The HTML is invalid because headings require a larger font-size than body text
The browser will refuse to render repeated identical font sizes on one page
There is no visual hierarchy, so the viewer has no signal for what to read first
The page will automatically fail a color-contrast accessibility check

prompt: You're building a type scale from a 16px base using a ratio of 1.25, which generates 16, 20, 25, 31... What size comes right after 20px in this scale?
Why does pairing Playfair Display (a serif display face) with Source Sans Pro (a sans-serif body face) read as a more deliberate choice than pairing Arial headings with Helvetica body text?
choices: Arial and Helvetica are so visually similar that the switch looks accidental, while Playfair Display and Source Sans Pro contrast clearly enough to read as a decision
Serif fonts always render faster in the browser than sans-serif fonts
Source Sans Pro is not licensed for use in page headings
Playfair Display and Source Sans Pro are the only two fonts installed on every operating system by default
